\*\*YOU’RE NOT ALONE. FIND MOM FRIENDS.\*\*

Welcome to Peanut, the ultimate mom app connecting women through all stages of motherhood, helping you find your village.

Join over 5 million women on Peanut to find mom friends, ask questions about your baby, and get support when you need it most. Whether you’ve moved to a new neighborhood, or you’re just looking for friends who get it, Peanut provides access to a community of moms ready to share advice and experiences.

Finding mom friends at a similar stage in life is easy on Peanut!

\*\*FIND MOM FRIENDS WHO GET IT\*\*

👋 Meet: Swipe to meet local moms at every life stage.

💬 Chat: Match with a new mom friend and chat about anything, baby advice, or mom hacks.

👭 Groups: Join support groups for newborn baby care, toddler moms, and many more.

🤔 Ask: Seek advice on baby names, baby sleep, and more from your new mom friends.

💁‍♀️ Share: Share advice on everything from mom life to baby care. Discuss topics like baby name suggestions, newborn baby routines, and other milestones in your journey.

🫶🏼 Baby Milestones: Share your baby's milestones with other moms with babies at a similar stage.

👻 Incognito Mode: Ask anything anonymously, from sex as a new mom to dealing with baby tantrums or the challenges of being a single mom.

\*\*WE’VE GOT YOU\*\*

Don't worry, mama. Safety is embedded throughout the app to encourage caring, supportive, and purposeful connections among moms and women.

✔️ Verified Profiles: All profiles on Peanut are checked with selfie verification to ensure safety for all moms.

✔️ Zero Tolerance: We have zero tolerance for abusive behavior.

✔️ Sensitive Content Filters: Mask content that may be triggering, protecting moms.

✔️ Customized Feed: Personalize your feed to focus on what is important for you, baby care, or finding mom friends.

# Peanut App for Moms: Why It's a Must-Have

Motherhood can be an incredible journey — but it can also feel isolating at times. That’s where the Peanut app comes in! Designed to help moms connect, share advice and build a supportive community, Peanut is a game-changer for modern motherhood.

Founded by [Michelle Kennedy](https://michellekennedy.co/), a former executive at a dating app, Peanut takes inspiration from matchmaking technology to help moms find like-minded friends. Whether you're navigating pregnancy, dealing with toddler tantrums, or simply looking for someone who gets it, this app creates a safe and engaging space for moms to connect.

But Peanut is more than just a social networking platform. It offers community groups, discussion forums and expert advice on everything from baby care to parenting tips. Plus, features like a pregnancy tracker and registry builder make planning for a new baby even easier.

Ready to [learn more about Peanut](https://www.peanut-app.io/blog/what-is-peanut-app)? Let’s get started.

## How the Peanut App Works

Peanut makes it easy for users to sign up and start connecting. Here's a step-by-step guide on [how to use the Peanut app](https://www.peanut-app.io/blog/how-to-use-peanut-app):

- Download the Peanut App: Available in the App Store for both iOS and Android devices.

- Create an Account: Sign up using your email or a Facebook account to get started.

- Customize Preferences: Indicate your interests, parenting style and goals, whether you're looking to track pregnancy milestones, [seek baby advice](https://milk-drunk.com/category/podcast/) or connect with toddler moms.

- Explore the Community: Join topic-based groups, participate in discussions and browse profiles of moms with similar interests.

- Start Connecting: Engage with other moms, join conversations and schedule meetups with local moms to build in-person relationships.

- Stay Engaged: Participate in live chats, share experiences and find support on topics like mom loneliness, pregnancy sickness and mental health.

- Stay on Free or Upgrade to Premium: Unlock additional features such as exclusive discussion groups and expert-led Q&A sessions for more tailored support.


One of the standout features is the selfie verification process, which ensures a secure space for moms to share their experiences without worrying about privacy concerns. Peanut also integrates a registry builder, making it easier for new moms to track and organize baby essentials.

## Who Can Use the Peanut App?

Peanut is designed for a wide range of women, including:

- Expecting Mothers: Whether you're experiencing pregnancy sickness, tracking milestones or preparing for a newborn baby, Peanut connects you with others in the same stage of motherhood.

- New Moms: Receive support on newborn baby care, including sleeping routines, [formula feeding](https://www.hibobbie.com/products/bobbie-organic-infant-formula) tips, and adjusting to life with a baby.

- Toddler Moms: Find parenting hacks, strategies for managing baby tantrums and fun activities to engage your growing child.

- Single Moms: Connect with a supportive network of other single moms to share experiences and advice.

- Moms Looking for Local Connections: Find local moms in your area for playdates, coffee chats and community support.

- Women Facing Pregnancy Challenges: Discuss pregnancy issues, including fertility struggles, postpartum concerns and parenting a rainbow baby.

- Moms Seeking Practical Tips: Get recommendations on mom hacks to simplify daily parenting tasks.


Peanut also serves as an excellent platform for discussing mental health challenges, offering a safe and understanding environment where moms can [seek guidance](https://milk-drunk.com/category/mom-matters/) and reassurance.

## Features of the Peanut App for Moms

Peanut offers several features designed to support modern moms:

- Networking Opportunities: Easily find and connect with mom friends nearby to grow your support system.

- Community Guidelines: A structured, welcoming environment ensures that personal information remains safe and discussions stay respectful.

- Live Chats: Live audio conversations between members — called [Peanut Pods](https://www.peanut-app.io/blog/peanut-pods) — establish and build relationships.

- Privacy Measures: The app includes selfie verification for added security, helping maintain a trustworthy community.

- Meetups & Events: Engage with local moms through in-person gatherings, virtual events and themed discussion groups.

- Educational Resources: Learn about baby care, pregnancy issues, mental health, newborn routines and helpful mom hacks.

- Discussion Groups: Find groups focused on specific topics like baby names, newborn baby care and balancing work and motherhood.

- Registry Builder: A tool that helps expectant moms organize baby essentials and plan for their growing family.


Peanut also features tools like the [Chinese gender predictor](https://www.peanut-app.io/chinese-gender-predictor), making it a fun and interactive platform for expectant moms. Whether you need a place to network, vent, ask questions or simply [connect with other like-minded moms](https://medium.com/@kimdelaro/i-tried-the-peanut-app-for-moms-heres-what-happened-900bee47d888), Peanut has something for everyone.

## How the Peanut App Empowers Moms

Peanut helps reduce mom loneliness by creating a safe and supportive space for moms to:

- Receive Expert Advice: Get reliable baby advice and parenting tips from experienced moms and professionals.

- Discover Parenting Hacks: Learn creative mom hacks to simplify daily routines and manage hot-mess-days with ease.

- Access Pregnancy & Newborn Resources: Find guidance on everything from baby names to setting up your registry builder.

- Build Lasting Friendships: Connect with a community of loving Peanut moms who offer emotional support and encouragement.

- Meet Other Local Moms: Join local groups to expand your network and form meaningful relationships.


Additionally, the platform allows moms to share advice on postpartum recovery, balancing work and family life and navigating common parenting challenges such as baby tantrums, [feeding concerns and transitions](https://www.hibobbie.com/blogs/bobbieu/when-do-babies-stop-drinking-formula), and pregnancy issues.

## Peanut App vs. Other Parenting Apps

How does Peanut stand out from other apps?

- Community-Focused vs. Traditional Social Media: More personal and mom-centric than a Facebook group, [fostering real connections.](https://www.peanut-app.io/blog/get-more-connections-on-peanut-app)

- Authentic Parenting Tips vs. Generic Advice: Get real mom-to-mom insights tailored to your needs.

- Local Connections vs. Nationwide Platforms: Meet local moms and [build meaningful friendships](https://amyboyington.com/peanut-app-review/) beyond the screen.

- Women’s Health Support vs. Generic Wellness: Find resources focused on mental health, pregnancy and postpartum recovery.

- Smart Matchmaking vs. Random Networking: Designed like a matchmaking app to help like-minded moms form deeper relationships.


Unlike [other parenting apps](https://canvasbusinessmodel.com/blogs/competitors/peanut-app-competitive-landscape), Peanut prioritizes meaningful relationships and provides a structured space where moms can get support without being overwhelmed by larger social media platforms.

## Is the Peanut App Right for You?

The Peanut app is more than just a place to chat — it's a must-have for every mom! If you're looking for a safe, inclusive and engaging community, [Peanut users rave](https://www.peanut-app.io/editorial/peanut-app-reviews) about how the app helps them navigate the ups and downs of motherhood.

Peanut is an invaluable resource for moms seeking friendship, advice and a place to share their parenting journeys. Whether you're a new mom, expecting or have older kids, Peanut has something for you.

Ready to find your new mom friend? [Download the app](https://www.peanut-app.io/download) and start connecting today!

Peanut App

**Peanut,** a product of Peanut App Ltd.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-2) is an online community for women who are planning to become [pregnant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pregnancy "Pregnancy"), women who are pregnant, women who have had children, and women who are experiencing [menopause](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menopause "Menopause"). Profiles of potential friends are displayed to users who can swipe up to show intent to connect.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-Romper-3) Users can also connect via discussion threads, groups, and live audio conversations. The app allows users to select their stage of life[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-4) (trying to conceive, pregnancy, motherhood, or menopause), so as to meet women at a similar life stage, and to discover relevant content.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-5)

Peanut was founded by Michelle Kennedy shortly after she left [Bumble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bumble "Bumble"),[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-6) a female-first dating app.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-7) She has described Peanut as, "the app she wishes she had when she first became a mother".[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-8)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-9)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-10)

## History

Peanut was initially launched in 2017 for mothers and pregnant women.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-11) The app focuses on helping users find others with shared interests, such as spoken languages, occupations, and hobbies.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-12) It also displays a woman's life stage, such as the age of her children, or the stage of pregnancy.

In 2018, it launched a community discussion feature that intended to give women an "alternative to other social platforms".[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-13) In 2019, it started to serve women who are trying to conceive.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-14)

In April 2021, it integrated live audio, in response to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), and the restrictions around in-person socializing.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-15)

in September 2021, it started to include women who are navigating perimenopause, [menopause](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menopause "Menopause"), and postmenopausal.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-16) Although it had initially catered for younger women navigating into new families, a large number of users had undergone surgically or chemically induced menopause due to medical conditions.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-17)

In July 2021, Peanut launched an investment micro fund, Peanut StartHER,[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-18) focused on investing in women-owned businesses, as well as other historically excluded founders.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-19)

## Operation

The Peanut app is a social network exclusively for women, focusing on topics of [pregnancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pregnancy "Pregnancy"), motherhood, [fertility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fertility "Fertility"), and menopause. It is available on [iOS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOS "IOS") and [Android](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Android_(operating_system) "Android (operating system)") devices. Users must prove their identity, in keeping with the primary function of in-app safety, and then they can create a profile to interact with other users.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-20)

For pregnant users, the “Bump Buddies” feature helps connect them with other Peanut users who have a similar due date, which aimed to help expecting mothers combat loneliness during the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-21)

Peanut users also have the option to join “Groups” ‒ sub-sections of users focused on specific topics, including (but not limited to) location, life stage, pregnancy due date, and interests or hobbies.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-Romper-3)

The live voice chat feature “Pods”, enables Peanut users to socialize without the pressure of photos or video chat. It offers features such as a muted audience of listeners who need to virtually raise their hand to speak, emoji reactions, and hosts who can moderate the conversations and invite people to speak.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peanut_App#cite_note-22)

# Meet The Tinder For Making New Mom BFFs

![profile picture of Anisa Arsenault](https://images.ctfassets.net/6m9bd13t776q/4SMby9mNTWq2qUOKgAgywQ/79c94361ba95205d335fe9990944ca4f/avatar.jpg?fit=thumb&h=140&w=140)

By [Anisa Arsenault,](https://www.thebump.com/author/anisaarsenault)Associate Editor

UpdatedFebruary 27, 2018

![Three mom friends sitting outside](https://media.front.xoedge.com/images/9c42b85c-69d4-4b51-9190-7559b25bffef~rs_1080.h?fm=webp&q=90)

Image:Getty Images

![](https://static.thebump.com/v2/shared/share-icons/pinterest-v1.png)

We can all swipe right on the idea of befriending moms you _actually_ want to be around. Whether you’re looking to widen your playgroup circle or find someone to connect with after daycare dropoff, a new app can make that a reality.

It’s called [Peanut](https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/peanut/id1178656034?mt=8), and it’s free. The brainchild of Bumble dating app creator Michelle Kennedy and her co-founder, Greg Orlowski, Peanut functions a lot like dating apps: Moms can swipe up to ‘wave’ at a potential friend in their area or swipe down to move to the next candidate. The criteria being assessed? Shared interests and ages of children (should you choose to schedule a playdate and not just a mom date). Plus, users can list their work schedules, which languages they speak and include fun decriptions of themselves: “fashion killa,” “spiritual gangsta” or “mom boss,” for example.

![](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Image:Peanut

![](https://static.thebump.com/v2/shared/share-icons/pinterest-v1.png)

“Peanut is designed to give women a network, \[and\] view motherhood as an adventure in the life of a woman,” reads a press release from the Peanut team. “Every step of Peanut is geared toward making it simple to reach out and connect in a friendly and accessible way.”

It also helps you _stay_ connected; moms can create groups within the app to suggest meetup ideas and send invitations to their friends. Most recently, Peanut added a feature called Pages, which serves as a sort of community board for moms across the app to chat about issues that matter most to them—money, relationships, current events, work/life balance—whether or not they ever meet in person. Like a combination of Slack, Twitter and Quora, a user’s feed will be populated with both content that’s trending and content that’s relevant to their interests.

![](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Image:Peanut

![](https://static.thebump.com/v2/shared/share-icons/pinterest-v1.png)

“We’re on a mission to build a community of women, who happen to be mamas,” the app’s description reads. Because motherhood isn’t your whole identity—but it _is_ something to bond over.

_Looking for more parenting apps?_ [Here’s a good one](https://www.thebump.com/a/baby-tech-baby-on-the-go-2017) for finding kid-friendly destinations.

H/T [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2017/02/09/peanut-is-a-tinder-like-app-for-making-new-mom-friends/)

# **I Tried the Peanut App for Moms — Here’s What Happened**

## My experience with using the latest motherhood app and how it can help first-time moms.

[![Kimberly Delarosa](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fill:32:32/1*efLB38u1ncx35mj7DarKqQ@2x.jpeg)](https://medium.com/@kimdelaro?source=post_page---byline--900bee47d888---------------------------------------)

[Kimberly Delarosa](https://medium.com/@kimdelaro?source=post_page---byline--900bee47d888---------------------------------------)

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*DFDZRhhVQ5kYodheKAXKlg.png)

I gave birth in March of 2020. As a first-time mother, having a baby at the peak of a global health pandemic was not something I prepared for at all.

My restrictions as a new mom with a newborn were magnified, and things like help and people coming over to see me were stripped away by quarantine. The first year with my son, I felt like I was on an island by myself without a clue on how to be a mom.

Every night, I’d ask myself countless questions like “Is this how life is going to be now?” and “How the hell am I going to do this?” The walls felt like they were closing in day after day, and I never felt so lonely in my life.

One day, while scrolling through social media, I stumbled on a post by Laura Prepon, famously known for her starring role in Orange Is the New Black. Prepon spoke about this new app for moms called [Peanut](https://www.peanut-app.io/).

Curious enough and looking for any lifeline, I decided to give it a try. Little did I know the [Peanut app](https://www.peanut-app.io/) would become the lifesaver I needed in the time of COVID-19. Here’s my review of [Peanut: the app for moms](https://www.peanut-app.io/).

### **How It Works**

The [Peanut app](https://www.peanut-app.io/) is an online community where women in all stages of life can ask questions, find support, and connect with other like-minded women. It’s been dubbed the Tinder for moms.

Whether you’re navigating pregnancy, fertility treatments, or menopause, the [Peanut app](https://www.peanut-app.io/) is a safe space for women to share information and offer valuable, real-world advice. And the best part about it is that the app is free.

Yep, you read it right. The [Peanut app](https://www.peanut-app.io/) is free, user-friendly, and easy to navigate. I created my profile within a matter of minutes and was able to connect with different women instantly. There is also a section where you can find local mothers in your area so that you can meet up.

### **Connections**

The connections that you make on this app are unlike any other. Finding mom friends can be a challenge, especially if you are in different stages of motherhood.

With the [Peanut app](https://www.peanut-app.io/), you can find moms who are going through the same experience you’re going through, which makes the [Peanut app](https://www.peanut-app.io/) so powerful.

The first mom friend I met through [Peanut](https://www.peanut-app.io/) was Lodia. We both had our boys around the same time and were going through the throes of postpartum and burnout. And every night while my son was fast asleep, Lodia and I were talking to one another, venting our frustrations, and letting each other know that everything would be okay.

For a new mom, having that kind of support during those dark times was so crucial — she saved my mental health in so many ways. We reminded one another that things were going to be okay and to hang in there.

We were each other’s support in a crazy world, and I will never forget her. And we still speak to this day.

### **Community**

Let’s face it, finding mom friends as a new mom can feel intimidating. However, finding your tribe is essential.

In the words of comedian Ali Wong, “when you’re a mom on maternity, it’s like the Walking Dead: you just gotta hook up with a crew to survive.” But how the hell can you find your community or tribe under mandated quarantine restrictions?

It felt almost impossible, which is where the [Peanut app](https://www.peanut-app.io/) filled the need.

Through [Peanut](https://www.peanut-app.io/), you can connect with like-minded women easily with the variety of groups on their platform. Created by [Peanut](https://www.peanut-app.io/) members themselves, you can explore and meet so many mothers.

From book clubs, outdoor clubs, music lovers, wine lovers, career moms, stay-at-home moms, LGBTQIA moms, socially awkward moms, or moms in their 30s — the [Peanut app](https://www.peanut-app.io/) has got it all. For someone forced to stay isolated, this brought me the community I needed.

### **Final Thoughts**

When I signed up in April of 2020, I didn’t think this would have a massive impact on my life. In all honesty, I thought this was another social media platform where things get saturated.

I can wholeheartedly say that the [Peanut app](https://www.peanut-app.io/) has been a lifesaver for me. Without this app, I wouldn’t have the emotional support I desperately needed as a COVID mom. This app gave me a sense of hope, a sense that I was not the only mother who gave birth during this crazy time and was trying to navigate this new normal on her own.

There’s an army of COVID-19 mothers who are trying to navigate this new normal and provide the best life for their children, just like me. It’s great to find moms who know exactly what I’m going through, and with this app, we were all able to find each other. If you’re interested [, check out the Peanut app](https://www.peanut-app.io/) and see for yourself.
